role: reduce the tied divisor event to a known theorem guaranteeing that a specific integer has a divisor in a specified class
missing_theorem: A published theorem T: for every N in a family 𝓕 that contains, for each prime p ≡ 1 (24), at least one 4Cp+1 (some C = C(p)), N has a divisor d ≡ −1 (mod 4C). The known existence shapes are product forcing (N ≡ −1 (mod m) ⇒ a prime factor ∉ ker), which is empty here because 4Cp+1 ≡ +1 (mod 4C), and Zsigmondy/Bilu–Hanrot–Voutier primitive divisors. A primitive divisor ℓ of a Lucas U_n(P,Q) satisfies ℓ ≡ (D/ℓ) (mod n), i.e. ℓ ≡ ±1 with the sign a quadratic character.
yield: ES (if such a T covered the (★) integers)
status_ref: Pass 1 U08 (arXiv phrase search: no hit); CLASS_FORCING Thm 2.1 (product/reciprocity forcing sees only [p] in G, never the class of a divisor of an integer ≡ 1); FRONTIER §3 M-pattern table (no every-n polylog theorem known, (J)103)
barrier: B2 + 'reciprocity forces parity never class': every known divisor-existence theorem either forces via the total product (useless at N ≡ 1) or via cyclotomic/Lucas rank of apparition, which brings the class down to ±1 mod n but leaves the sign as a quadratic character (T1-type parity bit)
new_ingredient: Lucas primitive divisors cut φ(4C) classes to {±1}; the remaining bit is (D/ℓ). This is a real class-reduction mechanism, but it needs 4Cp+1 to share a primitive divisor with some U_{4C}(P,Q), which restates 'ℓ has rank 4C'
next: Write the Lucas reading at C = 1: U₄(1, −2p) = 4p + 1 and D = 8p + 1, so a prime ℓ | 4p+1 has ℓ ≡ (8p+1/ℓ) (mod 4). Check whether this is a tautology (it is: ℓ ≡ ±1 mod 4 always) before trying 4C > 4.
note: The literature mining itself returned nothing in Pass 1. The only theorem family that controls the class of a divisor (not just its parity) is primitive divisors, and only up to ±1. Recorded as information on what a class-controlling input looks like.

Here, for (★): M = 4uC−1 | p+u, M ≡ 3 (4) and M ≡ −1 (mod u) give (M/p) = (p/M) = −(u/M) = −1, so any (★) certificate is a QNR read off without factoring (checked: scripts/z52d_avenue_Q16_qnr.py, all 15714 certificates at primes p ≡ 1 (4) < 2·10⁴).
